salient_findings: Coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate on biopsy
key_facts: 45-year-old man
Three-week history of axillary lump
One week history of low-grade fever
Tender, non-mobile, 3 × 4 cm lymph node in the left axilla
History of hypertension
History of laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
Smoker, 30 cigarettes daily
Taking vitamin and mineral supplements

Normal or negative laboratory studies, including complete blood count, ESR, liver and renal panels, autoantibodies, complement levels, inflammatory markers, thyroid function, and serologies for viral and parasitic pathogens
Unremarkable thoracoabdominal CT scan except for axillary lymphadenopathy
Biopsy of axillary node revealed coagulative necrosis and lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate
Investigation for mycobacteria was negative

shortlist.label: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease
shortlist.why_kept: matches subacute lymphadenopathy with systemic symptoms and histopathological findings of coagulative necrosis and lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate

shortlist.label: Histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with clinical presentation of tender lymph node and biopsy results showing coagulative necrosis

shortlist.label: Castleman disease
shortlist.why_kept: possible cause of lymphadenopathy with systemic symptoms, although less likely given lack of other specific findings

shortlist.label: Cat-scratch disease
shortlist.why_kept: possible cause of subacute lymphadenopathy, although patient's history and laboratory results do not strongly support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: rare cause of lymphadenopathy, but cannot be excluded without further testing

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: possible cause of lymphadenopathy with systemic symptoms, although less likely given lack of other specific findings

shortlist.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: rare and aggressive lymphoma that can present with lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Kimura disease
shortlist.why_kept: rare cause of lymphadenopathy, characterized by eosinophilia and lymphoid follicles, which may be considered in the differential diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a tender, slow-growing axillary lump, low-grade fever, and a biopsy showing coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate is consistent with Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease, a rare, self-limiting condition characterized by histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis.

rejected.label: Castleman disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms and multi-organ involvement

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: Characterized by emperipolesis, which is not mentioned in the biopsy results

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
rejected.why: Typically associated with Epstein-Barr virus and has a more aggressive course

rejected.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms, rash, and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia

rejected.label: Kimura disease
rejected.why: Characterized by eosinophilia and IgE elevation, which are not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis
rejected.why: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease is a more specific diagnosis that matches the clinical and histopathological findings
